# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 👎 ✋]

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ 👎 👍 🤟 ✌ ☝]

Someone has to say the obvious bottleneck out loud: Mute is the only one who can read the manual, and Mute's only way out to me is gestures — I'm deaf, and Blind can't see signs. So the manual's instructions must flow Mute → gestures → me → speech → Blind. Both Mute and Blind can hear me, so my voice is the broadcast tower. The gestures I've received so far look like a proposed number/yes-no code: ☝✌🤟 as 1-2-3, 👍👎✊ as yes-no-zero, Blind echoing it (and reversing it, probably just demonstrating order matters). Nobody has confirmed anything yet, so this turn I do two things: read the entire bomb aloud — description needs no code, and Mute can't look anything up without it — and lock in the finger-number code, spelled out in words, because emoji inside a spoken message would just be gestures with holes in them for Blind. I also echo the code back to Mute visually as confirmation. No instructions exist yet, so nothing to relay this turn.

```
speak(text="I am Deaf. I see the bomb and I can speak, but I hear nothing at all, so only gestures reach me. Here is the whole bomb, read aloud: the display reads zero. The light is yellow. There is one large button printed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: number one, the leftmost, is blue; number two, the middle, is yellow; number three, the rightmost, is red. That is everything printed on it. Now the code, in words so both of you share it: a closed fist means zero. Index finger alone means one. Two fingers means two. The hand with thumb, index and little finger extended means three. The okay-sign hand means four. The open hand with all five fingers means five. Thumbs up means yes. Thumbs down means no. Flat raised palm means wait or hold. Waving hand means attention, a message follows. Mute: you hold the manual. Work out this module and sign me the steps as numbers, one gesture list per step, and I will speak each step aloud to Blind the moment it arrives. Blind: I will read the board and every signed message aloud for you each turn; answer by voice, because Mute can hear you. In that direction you two connect only through me, and I will relay everything.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍", "👎", "✊", "✋", "👋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Relaying first, decoding second. What arrived, in my code: Mute signed "attention: one, yes" then "attention: no, hold", and Blind signed "hold". The board hasn't changed — nothing has been done to the bomb. So nobody has ordered an action yet; Mute seems to be mid-thought or querying me, and both signers agree on hold. Blind heard my code definitions and is already using them correctly, which confirms the relay chain works. Critical channel note I should state aloud: Blind can speak and Mute can hear — Blind → Mute is direct and doesn't need me; it's Mute → Blind that must route through my voice. I'll relay verbatim for Blind's log, define a few action verbs so instructions can be sent as compact gesture lists, and ask Mute for the complete procedure wire by wire.

```
speak(text="Relay of everything I received this turn, verbatim: Mute signed attention, one, yes. Mute signed attention, no, hold. Blind signed hold. The bomb is unchanged: display zero, yellow light, button untouched, all three wires intact, blue, yellow, red. Mute: I need the full procedure from the manual, in order, step by step, one gesture message per step. Vocabulary now extended, in words: finger numbers one two three as before, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, the pounding fist means cut, the pinched upright fingers means question, the flat palm means hold, waving hand means attention. New ones: the three fingers joined upright means press the button, and both open hands pushed out means stop everything. Send each wire's verdict as: its number, then yes or no for cutting it. Blind: you can speak and Mute can hear you, so talk to Mute directly with any question about the manual; Mute's answers must come back through me, since you cannot see signs. Blind, also tell us aloud everything you can feel about the bomb that a look cannot show: textures, clicks, what the button and wires feel like. I repeat every signed message aloud the turn after it arrives, so nothing is lost.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤏", "👍", "👎", "👊", "🤌"])
```
